questions.question: If your truck or trailer catches fire, where should you park?

options.text: In a busy area near trees.
At a service station.
Near other vehicles.
In an open area.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an open area.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle catches fire, leave the road and stop right away. Park in an open area away from trees, plants, and other vehicles that could catch fire. Do not go to a service station.

questions.question: What is road rage?

options.text: Driving a motor vehicle to harm or assault others or their vehicles.
Driving a motor vehicle that is unsafe.
Driving a motor vehicle that has not been inspected.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving a motor vehicle to harm or assault others or their vehicles.
questions.explanation: Aggressive driving means driving in a selfish, bold, or pushy way. Road rage means driving a motor vehicle to harm or assault another driver or damage their vehicle.

questions.question: Before looking under your vehicle's hood during a pre-trip inspection, you should:

options.text: Use the parking brake and/or chock blocks on the wheels.
Leave the vehicle in a low gear.
Remove the battery.
Disconnect the radiator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the parking brake and/or chock blocks on the wheels.
questions.explanation: Before inspecting under the hood, engage the parking brake and/or place chock blocks under the wheels to keep the vehicle in place.

questions.question: Which agency helps coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards?

options.text: The National Response Center.
The Federal Containment Organization.
The United Center for Chemical Assistance.
The National Transportation Network.

questions.correctAnswerText: The National Response Center.
questions.explanation: The National Response Center helps police and firefighters coordinate emergency response to chemical hazards.

questions.question: If you think a road might be icing over, how can you check?

options.text: Guess based on the temperature.
Open the window and feel the mirror or antenna for ice.
Look at the road surface carefully.
Check the weather forecast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the window and feel the mirror or antenna for ice.
questions.explanation: Open your window and touch the side mirror, mirror support, or antenna. If you feel ice on these parts, the road is likely becoming icy too.

questions.question: If a vehicle has a vehicle inspection report, the driver should:

options.text: Not read it and find any issues themselves.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.
Read and review the report.
Skip the pre-trip inspection and rely only on the report.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read and review the report.
questions.explanation: Start a vehicle inspection by reading any previous inspection reports. The company should have already fixed any problems listed in the report.

questions.question: When going down a steep hill, shift to a lower gear:

options.text: Before you start the downhill grade.
After you have already started the downhill grade.
As far down the hill as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before you start the downhill grade.
questions.explanation: Shift to a lower gear before you begin going downhill. Gravity will increase your vehicle's speed on hills, so be prepared.

questions.question: When driving in fog, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Drive on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, reduce your speed to stay safe.

questions.question: What are baffled tanks?

options.text: Tanks that do not prevent liquid from surging forward and backward.
Tanks with dividers that have holes, letting liquid move between sections.
Tanks that remove air through a valve.
Tanks that are easier to unload.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tanks with dividers that have holes, letting liquid move between sections.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have dividers with holes that help control liquid movement. They reduce forward and backward surge, but side-to-side movement may still happen.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving.
Drink coffee.
Stop and rest.
Drive faster to finish sooner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest.
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, the only safe choice is to stop and get sleep. Using caffeine or other stimulants can be dangerous because extreme tiredness may follow when they wear off.

questions.question: When loading liquid cargo into a tank with bulkheads, where should most of the weight go?

options.text: At the top of the tank.
In the middle of the tank.
At the rear of the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle of the tank.
questions.explanation: Do not place too much weight at the front or rear of the vehicle when filling a tank with bulkheads.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Open the radiator cap quickly.
Touch the radiator cap without gloves.
Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and let it cool before adding coolant. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: If you notice an unusual noise or feeling while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Ignore it and keep driving.
Hope the vehicle is okay until another driver takes over.
Check it out and find the right solution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check it out and find the right solution.
questions.explanation: If you see, hear, smell, or feel anything unusual while driving, have it checked out right away.

questions.question: Explosive materials are most likely classified as a ____ hazard.

options.text: Class 1
Class 3
Class 6
Class 7

questions.correctAnswerText: Class 1
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are items that can cause explosions or fires.

questions.question: Trailers made before 1975:

options.text: Must have spring brakes.
Do not need to have spring brakes.
Are unsafe to drive.
Cannot be used on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers made before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: Portable tanks:

options.text: Cannot be removed from a vehicle.
Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
Are permanently attached to a vehicle.
Should not be used.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are not permanently attached to a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Cargo tanks stay on a vehicle at all times. Portable tanks are bulk packaging that are not permanently attached to a vehicle.

questions.question: When driving under bridges and overpasses, you should:

options.text: Trust that the posted clearance height is correct.
Assume the posted clearance height may not be correct.
Measure the height before going through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the posted clearance height may not be correct.
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted height signs are accurate. Road resurfacing or snow buildup can change the actual clearance. If unsure your vehicle will fit, slow down and find another route.

questions.question: During the pre-trip inspection, after starting the engine, the coolant temperature should:

options.text: Go down.
Go up slowly.
Stay the same.
Jump up quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go up slowly.
questions.explanation: Watch the gauges after starting your engine. The coolant temperature should gradually rise to normal operating range.

questions.question: A person supervising the loading or unloading of a tank must do all of the following except:

options.text: Stay alert.
Stay within 25 feet of the tank.
Wear a chemical suit.
Know the hazards of the materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear a chemical suit.
questions.explanation: The supervisor must stay alert, have a clear view, stay within 25 feet, know the hazards, know emergency procedures, and be able to move the tank if needed.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not inform others of their intentions.
Only use turn signals if another vehicle is beside them.
Not use a turn signal if a lane change will be obvious.
Always use turn signals to tell others their intentions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use turn signals to tell others their intentions.
questions.explanation: Always use proper signals to let others on the road know what you plan to do.
